scope: General Ar'nock solid-state electromechanical maintenance, fabrication, service documentation, propulsion/transit refit, and recertification grammar.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Family-specific gravity sensitivity, predictive safety sensing, emergency de-transit, maturity-scaled redundancy, realistic mathematical limits, and generations-deep technical documentation.

technologyInvariants: General Ar'nock machinery defaults to solid-state electromechanical modular construction.
General computation defaults to solid-state silicon.
Piezoelectric sensing and actuation are characteristic but do not substitute for family-specific exotic sensors.
Complete functional assemblies are the normal field-service boundary.
Bioprinting is secondary support technology unless a subsystem-level source establishes a biological exception.
Species identity does not select an FTL family.
Service documentation never promotes DERIVED or PROPOSED values to CONFIRMED canon.

smallResonanceShift.use: small perturbation interpretation; not unique fault identification

safeguards: physical fit does not imply functional compatibility
functional compatibility does not imply calibration equivalence
missing calibration does not mean zero error
unknown service history does not mean serviceable

propulsionTransitRecertification.interventionEquation: t_int = t_sensor + t_solver + t_decision + t_command + t_actuate + t_exit + t_clear + t_margin
propulsionTransitRecertification.portalRule: Use mouth admission, synchronization, exit, and recovery timing; do not invent along-route hull velocity.
propulsionTransitRecertification.familyRule: Recertification is adapted to the selected family only after family identity is independently resolved.

minimumSequence: perform static electrical and insulation tests
record installed and removed module ancestry
returnToService.acceptanceRule: Return to service requires evidence, not absence of an alarm.

generatorRules: Emit a discoverable Maintenance / Service block for every substantial Ar'nock system.
List service boundary before repair procedure.
List required tools and evidence before declaring a module repairable.
Prefer module exchange over speculative component repair unless depot/foundry capability is explicitly present.
Preserve original module identity, replacement identity, calibration ancestry, and refit authority separately.
Do not generate numeric tolerances, torque values, resonance bands, latency limits, or service intervals without source or explicit labeled engineering control.
Do not use piezoelectric observations as unique fault diagnoses without corroborating evidence.
Do not treat a successful self-test as equivalent to thermal, timing, or family-specific transit certification.
Do not use biological repair tooling for general solid-state machinery unless subsystem provenance requires it.
Do not infer FTL family from Ar'nock machinery style.
